beginner.summary: For developers and data engineers who know Python or Java and SQL and are new to Apache Beam. Covers the Beam model (pipelines, PCollections, PTransforms), ParDo and DoFn, grouping and combining, side inputs and tagged outputs, schemas and type hints, event time, windows, triggers and late data, unit testing, the Java SDK basics, running on the DirectRunner, Prism and Dataflow, and a batch log-analytics capstone.
prerequisites: Writes working Python 3 functions and classes, or Java 17 classes, and uses a terminal and a virtual environment or Maven
Reads and writes SQL aggregations with GROUP BY and joins
Has a laptop that can run Python 3 with pip and, for the Dataflow days, a Google Cloud project with billing enabled and the gcloud CLI installed
outcomes: Explain the Beam model and build batch pipelines in the Python SDK using core transforms, windowing and side inputs
Write and run unit tests for pipelines with TestPipeline, assert_that and TestStream
Run the same pipeline on the DirectRunner, Prism and Dataflow by changing pipeline options only
Deliver a tested batch pipeline that parses logs, aggregates results and writes files

intermediate.summary: For engineers who can build and test basic Beam pipelines and now need production-grade batch and streaming work. Covers composite transforms, state and timers, custom combiners, streaming triggers, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, file formats, dead-letter handling, TestStream, enrichment, Java annotations and Beam SQL, Dataflow streaming and Flex Templates, the Flink runner, cross-language Kafka I/O, Beam YAML, observability and a streaming capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the beginner material or builds batch Beam pipelines with ParDo, GroupByKey, side inputs and windowing in Python or Java
Has a Google Cloud project with Pub/Sub, BigQuery, Cloud Storage and Dataflow enabled and the gcloud and bq CLIs configured
Uses Docker and a Git repository, and can read JSON and Avro schemas
outcomes: Build stateful, timer-driven and streaming pipelines with correct windows, triggers and late-data handling
Read and write Pub/Sub, BigQuery, files and Kafka reliably, with dead-letter outputs for bad records

advanced.summary: For senior data engineers who run Beam in production on Dataflow and Flink. Covers the portability framework, splittable DoFns, watermark and late-data strategy, exactly-once and idempotent sinks, large-state patterns, fusion and skew tuning, coders and memory, Dataflow troubleshooting, updates, security, Flink runner operations and tuning, custom containers, RunInference, custom connectors, benchmarking with Nexmark, platform governance, upgrades and a multi-runner capstone.
prerequisites: Has operated at least one streaming Beam pipeline with state, timers and windows, and uses Dataflow or Flink for real workloads
Reads Java and Python stack traces and Cloud Logging output and uses Docker, gcloud and IAM confidently
Understands Pub/Sub or Kafka delivery guarantees and at-least-once versus exactly-once semantics
outcomes: Diagnose and fix performance, skew, memory and stuck-job problems on Dataflow and Flink using metrics and logs
Build correct connectors, splittable DoFns and idempotent sinks that tolerate retries
Operate production jobs safely: updates, drains, security hardening, container builds and version upgrades
Design a governed multi-team Beam platform that runs the same pipelines on Prism, Dataflow and Flink
